name: seal-notation
title: Seal Notation
card: Write 32-byte hashes (sha-256 κ, BLAKE3 labels, Merkle roots, keys) as seals — one 26-character word from five scripts with an arithmetic check, via the pinned Sigil encoding — on web pages, in a spellbook-style listing, behind a page-wide toggle, and in a paste-and-check reader…
brief:
Write 32-byte hashes (sha-256 κ, BLAKE3 labels, Merkle roots, keys) as seals — one 26-character word from five scripts with an arithmetic check, via the pinned Sigil encoding — on web pages, in a spellbook-style listing, behind a page-wide toggle, and in a paste-and-check reader that says where a hash sits in a community's record. Use when hashes must be read, compared, copied or photographed by people, when a page should offer "show hashes as seals", or when building a seal reader or lookup.

A truncated hex hash has no check and can be imitated cheaply. A **seal** is the whole 32 bytes as one word of 26 characters, no two alike, selected whole by a double-click, with a check: one misread or changed character, or two swapped, cannot decode. The algorithm stays beside it (sha-256 unless marked).

- A page shows hashes people compare by eye. - Someone asks for "the hashes as sigils/seals", a toggle, a spellbook listing, or a "paste a hash, find it" page.
